messages:
anya.r: quick question for the group — before we expose remediation hints to end customers, do we require an explicit tenant opt-in? thinking about privacy/usage-telemetry concerns and some customers not wanting actionable guidance surfaced.

matt.b: curious — which hints do you mean? the `remediation_token` we sketched last week?

anya.r: yes. tokens like `errors.rate.limit.reduce_parallelism` that drive a console CTA or SDK helper. payload example: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMIT",
    "status": 429,
    "message": "rate limit exceeded",
    "exposure_level": "user_visible",
    "remediation_token": "errors.rate.limit.reduce_parallelism",
    "meta": {
      "suggested_parallelism": 4
    }
  }
}
```

sylvia.h: I like the idea of opt-in. We could model it as a tenant setting in Console: Error Hints = [none | admin-only | customer-visible]. That avoids header shenanigans and is auditable.

aiden.c: headers are simpler for per-call control (X-Redwood-Expose-Errors: minimal|full), but proxies / cdns may strip them. tenant-level flag is safer for long-term.

matt.b: operational concern: if we change payload shape some SDKs will parse unknown fields and assume actions. Need compatibility guarantees.

anya.r: compatibility plan: additive schema only, `exposure_level` defaults to `internal`. SDKs can opt-in to parse `remediation_token`. We'll publish a token catalog and semver the error schema.

sylvia.h: telemetry note: we must avoid high-cardinality from freeform tokens. whitelisting a catalog + token IDs is mandatory. Also we should record `token_id` (stable small string) not full localized text.

aiden.c: agree. instrument events: `error.exposure_level`, `error.token_id`, `ui.remediation_click` (bool + tenant_id), and `error.route_context` (admin-only). Keep token_id cardinality < 200.

matt.b: how does the console translate token -> CTA text/runbook? mapping in control plane? RBAC gating?

anya.r: mapping stored server-side in token registry. Console fetches token catalog (TTL cache) and i18n strings. For admin-only runbooks we only return an admin_url if the caller has admin scope. For public CTAs, we surface localized short action text only.

sylvia.h: rollout idea: 3-stage. 1) admin-only token visibility. 2) SDKs can parse tokens but UI remains off by default. 3) expose CTAs to customers for tenants that opt-in. Gate each stage with telemetry checks.

aiden.c: what telemetry checks?

anya.r: suggested metrics: 
- `cta_click_rate` (per token)
- `post_cta_retry_success_rate` (did suggested action reduce retries/errors)
- `error_churn_rate` (spurious errors after token surfaced)
- `token_catalog_miss_rate` (SDKs calling for unknown token ids)
- `exposed_error_pct` (portion of errors with exposure_level != internal)

matt.b: also add `unexpected_behavior_incidents` (pager triggers) to gate. If CTA causes more load (e.g., everyone reduces batch size causing throughput drop) we should roll back quickly.

sylvia.h: A/B experiment idea: randomly enable customer-visible CTAs for 5% of tenants, measure downstream user-visible metrics (retries down, latency changes), and compare. Keep experiment short (2 weeks) unless low volume.

aiden.c: telemetry payload size — are we ok adding `token_id` to every error event? sampling will be needed. Maybe only tag top-level errors or sample 1/10 by default; for admin tiers we keep full fidelity.

anya.r: agreed. sampling config per-tier. Admin telemetry retains `route_context` and full token ids. Public telemetry samples token occurrences.

matt.b: question on token lifecycle: how do we retire a token without breaking older SDKs?

anya.r: tokens are versioned. token id stays stable but maps to a new canonical token version. We'll keep a compatibility window (90 days) where old token behavior is retained and emit `token_deprecation` events in telemetry and control plane.

sylvia.h: console UX: minimal CTA in error banner + "More info" expands with suggested steps. For admin view show runbook link and route-level hints. I'll prototype a compact mobile-friendly banner.

aiden.c: infra: runtime schema change required to accept optional `exposure_level` + `remediation_token`. I'll add a non-breaking parser and a feature-guard flag `error_ext_v1`.

deploy-bot: feature flag created: `error_ext_v1` (staging).

matt.b: security check: ensure remediation_token cannot be used to craft URLs that leak internal endpoints. Runbook mapping should be server-side and return only the allowed public URL or admin URL based on RBAC.

anya.r: yes, tokens map to opaque runbook ids. clients never receive raw internal links unless admin. We'll also strip debug `route_context` from public responses.

sylvia.h: one more product ask: add an opt-out banner for tenants who previously opted-in but want to revert. Console setting should include a brief privacy/telemetry note.

aiden.c: engineering tasks: add schema parsing, token registry service, telemetry tags, and feature flag wiring. testing: synthetic `ui.remediation_click` events to validate alerts.

matt.b: i'll own the runtime change. anya.r will own the control-plane token registry. sylvia.h will do console mocks. aiden.c will do telemetry + sampling.

anya.r: action items:
- anya.r: create RFC for token registry + opt-in model (due EOD Wed)
- matt.b: PR for non-breaking parser + feature flag (staging)
- sylvia.h: console mockups for admin + customer banners
- aiden.c: telemetry schema + sampling proposal
- deploy-bot: enable `error_ext_v1` in staging for ABC tenants

deploy-bot: RFC placeholder created: https://go/redwood/rfc/error-cta-optin-2026 (assign: anya.r, matt.b, sylvia.h, aiden.c)

anya.r: thanks all. If no objections i'll file the RFC and start the token catalog skeleton.

matt.b: no objections from me. :+1:

sylvia.h: :+1:

aiden.c: :+1:

anya.r: closing thread — will ping when RFC link is up.
